events.name: Drag queen kareoke
events.description:
Beah Hazard is taking over the Lounge mic — and honey, nobody's safe. This is karaoke for the people: your coworker belting Whitney off-key, your best friend finally doing that Selena number she's been threatening for years, strangers turned duet partners by the second chorus. Messy, glorious, unfiltered.

Between the chaos, Beah and her drag sisters serve full-blown live performances — the kind that stop conversations mid-sentence and get the whole room screaming. Real drag, real vocals, real drama, no half-stepping.

September 2nd, 7pm, Azúcar's Lounge — dim lights, cold drinks, a crowd ready to lose it over a good chorus. Sign up to sing or just come watch the show unfold. Either way, you're leaving with a story.

events.name: Drag Brunch de Reinas
events.description:
Summer just got sinful, mamis. Drag Brunch de Reinas struts onto the Main Floor with four reinas ready to work every inch of that stage. Cynthia Marche serves gowns that could stop traffic. Frívola Montes de Oca brings the chaos and the comedy. Ana Deborah owns the room like she pays rent here. Abele Fantasy? That body alone deserves a round of applause — and a mimosa refill.

Doors crack open at 9:30am. VIP queens meet-and-greet runs 10–11am — get close, get a photo, get flirty before the show even starts. Brunch pours from 10am to 2pm, mimosas flowing like it's nobody's business. The main show — full drag, full glam, full innuendo — hits 11am to 1pm. Then photos with the queens from 1–2pm, so you can prove to your friends this actually happened.

Stick around for the after party, 2–4pm, when brunch energy melts into afternoon chaos — the good kind. Bottomless drinks, bold queens, and a room that gets hotter by the hour. This is summer, Latinx-style: bright, filthy fun, and completely unforgettable.

Get your tickets now, reinas — this brunch sells out faster than a compliment from Frívola.

events.name: Beyoncés birthday party drag show
events.description:
Halo up, mis abejas — September 5th belongs to the Queen. Azúcar's Main Floor transforms into a shrine of gold sequins and honey light as we celebrate Beyoncé's birthday AND the 20th anniversary of B'Day, the album that told y'all not to test her. Rohla Blunt takes the mic to host, with Dillon holding down the room right beside her, for a night that hits as hard as "Ring the Alarm" — because this is not a drill.

Expect drag performances so sickening they should come with a warning label, a catwalk contest for the brave ones ready to strut like they're in the "Déjà Vu" video, and Yoncé Trivia that will separate the real Beyhive from the casual fans. The DJ keeps the floor moving all night — Destiny's Child deep cuts, B'Day bangers, Renaissance heat, all of it.

Come dressed like you're headed to the Grammys or straight off the "Suga Mama" set — either way, Bey would approve. Want a table locked down before the honey light hits? Hit up Rohla Blunt or Dillon directly, or slide into our Facebook page — reservations are free, but they go fast.

Grab a drink, find your seat before the trivia starts, and get ready to scream every lyric like your life depends on it. Because tonight, at Azúcar, it kind of does.

events.name: Build your own Carabiner
events.description:
Forget scrolling for cute keychains — make one yourself. On September 6th, the Lounge transforms into a DIY playground packed with hundreds of charms, trinkets, and acrylic pieces just waiting to become your next signature accessory. Bag clip, keyring, water bottle dangle — whatever you're building it for, Jayme's got the vibe and the table set up so you can dig in, get creative, and walk out with something nobody else has.

This one's built for slowing down and connecting — pull up a seat, start sorting through trinkets, and strike up conversation with whoever's next to you doing the same. No pressure, no small talk required, just good music, good company, and a shared table full of tiny treasures. Azúcar's Lounge gets cozy for this one: think low light, easy chatter, and everyone heads-down on their own little masterpiece.

Best part? Every proceeds dollar goes right back into community events, so your new carabiner is basically a receipt for good karma. Come solo and leave with new friends, or bring your people and turn it into a craft night. Either way, you're building more than a keychain — you're building your corner of the community, one charm at a time.

events.name: Night of Kings; An All King Drag Show
events.description:
The lights go low and the bass goes dirty. Smoke curls under red spotlights as the Lounge transforms into a den of pure, unfiltered swagger — this is Night of Kings, and every corner of the room hums with sultry, punk-edged energy. Cherry Pop holds court as host, his charisma cutting through the haze like a blade, guiding the crowd through a night built entirely around the art of the drag king — studs and Kings serving looks sharp enough to cut glass.

Expect leather, grit, and grind — a parade of local kings serving sex appeal with a snarl, each one carving out their own slice of the spotlight. This lineup doesn't just bring heat, it brings laughs too — comedy bits woven between jaw-dropping numbers that'll have you gasping one minute and cackling the next. Some sets growl with rock riffs, some slink through slow-burn seduction, others detonate into pure punk chaos. The mood shifts song to song but the thesis stays the same: masculinity, unleashed and reimagined, dripping in confidence.

Grab a drink, find your spot in the dark, and let the Lounge close in around you. September 13th, 8pm — Azúcar's stage belongs to the kings tonight, and Cherry Pop isn't asking permission.
